summary: Octagonal steel light on a crib at the end of the Portage River breakwater, Keweenaw Bay: built 1919-20 to replace a 1911 pierhead light; automated in the 1950s; Coast Guard-owned and not open to visitors.

light.characteristic: fixed white flash every six seconds (2014 nomination; record had Fl G 4s)

lens.note: Fourth-order lens from the 1911 pierhead light, moved in 1920; removed around 2010 and replaced by a modern LED optic.

light.fog_signal: 6-inch siren (1920), later duophone, now electric fog signal keyed by VHF radio

structures.type: octagonal steel tower and circular lantern on a reinforced concrete base
structures.note: Steel tower about 30 ft high on a concrete base; record's 19.0 m is not confirmed (NRHP says about 90 ft above the lake bed; USLHS 31 ft to lantern centre).

structures.type: timber crib with concrete pier, filled with rock
power house, compressed-air plant, quarters for three keepers (shore end of breakwater)

structures.note: Discontinued and removed after the 1920 light was established.

access.note: Not open to public visitation; reached from shore along the breakwater (NRHP).

events.note: Portage Entry Light established to mark the offshore end of the breakwater; a pair of onshore range lights at the river mouth also erected
Federal government purchases the Keweenaw Waterway (August 1891)
Wooden 27 ft pierhead light with fog bell at the breakwater's offshore end
Two-story iron skeletal tower with a fourth-order Fresnel lens (fixed red) replaces the 1902 pierhead light
Bureau of Lighthouses plans electric lights and a taller light to replace the pierhead light
Construction of the new lighthouse begins (timber crib, concrete pier, steel tower)
Established as the Keweenaw Waterway Lower Entrance Light on 1 August 1920
Fourth-order lens transferred from the 1911 pierhead light
6-inch siren fog signal operated from shore by compressed air; power house and keepers' quarters on shore
Project completed; final completion set for 15 October 1920 (cost given by LighthouseFriends as $104,874.70)
About 1,500 ft of the fog-signal air pipe carried into the lake on 8 May; raised and reconnected by the keeper and crew; fog signal restored 10 May
Lighthouse Service keepers replaced by Coast Guard personnel (NRHP gives 1939; archive gives St. Andre to 1941)
Automated during the 1950s (decade only in the nomination)
Original fourth-order lens removed circa 2010 and replaced by an LED optic
Coast Guard deems the light excess and makes it available under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act (LighthouseFriends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1868 date is the Portage Entry Light at the breakwater's end, which was replaced by pierhead lights in 1902 and 1911 and by the present light in 1920. The 1868 and 1920 dates are both right for their structures.
Record's 1919 and 1920 dates match the nomination: construction began in 1919, the light was established 1 August 1920.
The archive gives St. Andre to 1941; the nomination says Lighthouse Service keepers ran the light until 1939 and Coast Guard personnel after. The sources do not settle the date.

notes_for_editor: Rich-enough station for a moderate story. Main spine: the 2014 NRHP nomination (digitised, full text read) and the Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1918-1924. (1) Name confusion: the 'Portage River Light' at Jacobsville (1869 onshore light, sold 1958, now a bed and breakfast) and the 'Portage River Pierhead Light' (1902, 1911) are different structures from this light; the story says so. (2) The 1920 Bulletin's main-light paragraph is badly OCR'd. The focal plane is read from 'G8' as 68 feet, consistent with USLHS (68 ft); the fog signal and lamp characteristic should be checked on the page image. The Bulletin describes the light as white and occulting, which does not match the record's Fl G 4s; the 2014 nomination says a white flash every six seconds. The story uses the nomination's description. (3) Tower height: record 19.0 m; USLHS 31 ft to lantern centre and 68 ft focal height; nomination about 90 ft above lake bed (incl. crib). Not resolved. (4) Keeper end dates: St. Andre to 1941 (USLHS) vs Lighthouse Service keepers to 1939 (NRHP). (5) Mattila: roster 'Charles I. Mattila'; Bulletin 1924 OCR 'Charley L Mattila'. (6) A 1912 Calumet News obituary (10 April 1912, p. 2, Chronicling America sn86086633) is headed 'Capt. Earl Edgerton ... Owner of Stone Quarry at Portage Entry' and mentions the Keweenaw waterway lighthouse in its OCR. It is only a name-and-place match with the roster's (Guy) Earl Edgerton (1868-1872); not used in the story. (7) The 53 roster entries and their 1868-1971 span come from roster.py's count, not from a single quotation. (8) The 2014 nomination is dated 23 January 2014; the record's nrhp_listed 2014 was not checked against the Register's listing date. (9) After the 2014 excess notice, the sources here do not say who owns the light now. (10) LighthouseFriends is used only for the 2014 excess notice and the cost figure, which the story does not print. (11) Page numbers 16-19 for the nomination were read from the form's page breaks; the reviewer should confirm. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 1920 Bulletin focal plane reads 'G8' in OCR (68 ft is also in the 2014 nomination); the 1924 Bulletin index gives 'Charley I. Mattila'; the 2016 conservancy award rests on LighthouseFriends alone; page images were not viewed.
